prompt.context: Your client is the CEO of a major English soccer team. He's called you while brimming with excitement after receiving news that Lionel Messi was looking for a new team. Players of Messi's quality rarely became available, and would surely improve any team. However, with COVID-19 restricting budgets, money would be tight and would need to generate a return.
prompt.question: He would like you to figure out what the right amount of money to offer would be.

clarifying_info.a: To win the European Championship within 3 seasons. Due to recent financial restrictions, all of their player acquisitions must be offset with new revenue within 5 years.

clarifying_info.q: How do soccer teams acquire players?
clarifying_info.a: In soccer transfers, the acquiring team buys out the new player for an agreed upon fee. After they pay that fee, they then agree a new annual contract with the player.

clarifying_info.q: How does the team make money?
clarifying_info.a: Have the candidate brainstorm revenue streams — do not give the answer directly.
Soccer is a global sport where a team strives to score more goals than their opponent.
He is in the conversation for greatest of all time. He contributed (scored or assisted) 55 goals last season.

exhibits.title: Recent Transfers of Top Forwards
exhibits.shows: A table of five recent top-forward transfers listing each player's name, age at time of transfer, goal contributions (goals + assists), transfer fee, and transfer year.

data.footnote: Goal contributions include goals and assists. European average for attacking players is 12; over 30 is considered elite.

framework: Messi assessment: quality (55 goal contributions vs. elite threshold of 30+), age/career arc (35 years old — fewer productive years), fit/willingness to join, cheaper alternatives
Valuation via market comparables: calculate transfer fee / goal contributions multiples from Exhibit 1; adjust for age
Financials — incremental revenue: ticket sales, food & beverage, TV/broadcast, sponsorship, jersey & merchandise
Financials — incremental costs: transfer/acquisition fee, annual salary + agent fees
ROI / payback period: does incremental profit cover the upfront fee within 5-year constraint?
Risks: injury risk increases with age, player may request a transfer out, style may not suit league, financial projections may be aggressive
Competitive response: could trigger a talent arms race among rivals

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 1, estimate an appropriate transfer fee for Messi using a market multiples approach.
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate transfer fee divided by goal contributions for each comparable: Ronaldo ~2x, Neymar ~10x, Mbappe ~10x, Aubameyang ~2x, Diego Costa ~2x. Average multiple is ~5x. A strong candidate recognizes that older players command lower multiples and uses ~2x (similar to Ronaldo at 33). Applying 2x (or the interviewer-provided guidance of 2.6x) to Messi's 55 goal contributions yields ~$143M.

math.setup: Transfer fee multiple = Transfer Fee / Goal Contributions. Messi's goal contributions = 55. Conservative multiple for a 35-year-old ≈ 2.6x (guided by interviewer).
steps: Older players (Ronaldo age 33) trade at ~2x; Messi is even older at 35 → use conservative multiple

questions.prompt: Calculate the team's current annual revenue across all major channels.
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify: ticket revenue, food & beverage, broadcast, sponsorship, jersey/merchandise. Strong candidates ask for data on each stream and set up clear calculations before computing.

math.setup: Given: 60,000 seats, 83.33% (5/6) fill rate, $50 ticket price, 25 home games, $10 F&B per fan, $150M broadcast, $50M sponsorship, 1M jerseys at $100 with 25% margin.

questions.prompt: Calculate the team's incremental annual revenue and costs if Messi is signed, then determine the payback period.
questions.guidance: Candidate must identify incremental revenue uplifts (sellout + $15 ticket premium, +10% broadcast, sponsorship doubles, Messi jersey effect net of cannibalization) and incremental costs (salary + agent fee). A good candidate finds payback just under 5 years. A great candidate flags risks around the aggressive revenue assumptions and Messi's age.

math.setup: New assumptions: 100% sellout, $65 ticket ($50+$15), broadcast +10% to $165M, sponsorship doubles to $100M, Messi jerseys 2M units (cannibalize 50% of existing 1M), salary $100M + 10% agent fee = $110M/year.
steps: New jersey: (2M new + 1M old × 50% kept) = 2.5M total × $100 × 25% = $62.5M
Payback period: $143M upfront / $30M per year ≈ 4.8 years (just under 5 years)
math.answer: Incremental profit $30M/year; payback period ~4.8 years — breaks even within the 5-year constraint

brainstorming.prompt: How does the soccer team make money? Brainstorm all revenue streams.

categories.name: Merchandise and licensing
ideas: Licensed video games and digital content

recommendation: The fair market value for Messi's transfer is approximately $143M, based on a conservative comparables multiple of 2.6x applied to his 55 goal contributions
At a $100M annual salary plus $10M in agent fees, the signing generates $30M incremental profit per year and breaks even in just under 5 years — within the client's 5-year constraint
Given the rarity of a player of Messi's caliber and the alignment with the European Championship goal, the client should proceed with the offer
risks: Revenue projections are aggressive — full sellout and doubled sponsorship may not materialize quickly
Messi is 35; injury risk increases with age, and productive seasons may be fewer than 5
High wages lock in a large cost base; if performance declines, the team cannot easily reduce salary
Messi could request a transfer out before the payback period concludes
next_steps: Conduct sensitivity analysis on the revenue model (e.g., partial sellout, 50% sponsorship uplift) to stress-test the payback period
Engage potential sponsors early to lock in incremental deals contingent on signing
Negotiate contract structure (e.g., performance bonuses, shorter initial term with options) to manage downside risk
